transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-05-06 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE); Samira Shah (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions Eng); Mark Rivera (Lumina CTO); Priya Desai (Lumina Platform Eng); James Liu (Lumina SRE); Sara Gomez (Lumina Product)

Summary: Quick follow-up after Monday's production incident (intermittent timeouts and 5xx spike). Focus on root cause, what Redwood traced, mitigations already applied (rate limiting, autoscaler tweak), and next steps to stabilize the POC.

00:00 Alex Kim: Thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick agenda - recap the incident, telemetry Samira pulled, mitigations deployed, and concrete next steps.
02:12 Mark Rivera: Yeah thanks. To recap from our side, Monday at ~10:03 UTC we saw a 15 minute window where a bunch of user requests started timing out then some 5xx errors popped up, downstream workers got throttled and our pipeline backed up.
04:05 Samira Shah: On Redwood's side we saw a burst of long tail latency on the model backend. Looks like concurrent KV cache evictions and heavy prefix cache misses coincided with a scheduled embeddings job. That forced more cold KV loads and some requests hit the 30s timeout.
06:30 James Liu: Our ingress logs show many clients doing immediate retries which just amplified the spike. Gateway queue depth increased and then a subset of model instances returned 503/oom-type 5xx around the peak.
08:40 Alex Kim: Ok, we pushed a temporary edge rate limiter and adjusted autoscaler thresholds so instances spin up earlier. Samira, can you give a quick telemetry summary?
10:15 Samira Shah: Sure - during the peak we saw ~2.4% error rate mostly 5xx, p99 latency jumped from ~600ms to ~28s for the worst route. The embeddings job caused sustained high mem pressure; combined with quant var switching it increased kernel selection time.
13:02 Priya Desai: That matches our internal metrics. That scheduled job was misconfigured to run on the hour and overlapped with high user traffic. We're changing the schedule. For embeddings-heavy jobs, any config suggestions to reduce p99 impact?
15:20 Samira Shah: We recommend isolating embeddings on a separate route and optionally a dedicated pool. Also batching windows for embeddings or pinning a quantized variant reduces memory pressure and cold-start cost.
17:45 Mark Rivera: About client retries - our libs currently do 3 immediate retries. Should we change that?
18:25 Alex Kim: Yes, switch to exponential backoff with jitter. Cap retries to 2 for user-facing requests, allow a bit more for background jobs but with idempotency keys. We pushed a client patch that defaults to jittered exponential backoff; Samira will share the PR.
21:10 James Liu: Can we set per-route soft rate limits and account-level burst tokens to prevent global hammering?
22:00 Samira Shah: Absolutely - Redwood supports per-route rate limits and token bucket burst controls. For the POC we'd recommend starting at a 200rps burst allowance with a steady-state 50rps for the embedding route, then tune after staging tests.
24:15 Priya Desai: We also need better visibility into queue time and kernel selection so we can detect pre-error buildup. Any tracing hooks?
25:05 Samira Shah: Use the Redwood tracing headers; sample 10% of user traffic and 100% on error. We'll send the tracing docs and a snippet to wire it into your tracing system.
27:30 Alex Kim: On mitigation we deployed a hotfix last night: lowered per-request memory cap, and adjusted autoscaler to start adding instances at 70% CPU. Early telemetry shows error rates dropping back to baseline.
30:10 Mark Rivera: That's good to hear. What's the rollback if we see regressions from the change?
31:00 Alex Kim: We have an auto-rollback policy that triggers if error rate increases beyond thresholds for 15 minutes. We can also fallback to a smaller model variant to reduce tail latency.
33:25 Priya Desai: Could Redwood run a targeted stress test against our staging so we can reproduce the behavior with the same load shape?
34:10 Samira Shah: Yes, we'll run a coordinated test. Please share your load shape and peak qps and we'll run a mirrored test tomorrow.
36:40 Mark Rivera: One more question - what's a good retry budget split between background jobs and user-facing requests?
38:00 Alex Kim: Background jobs can be slightly more aggressive but still use exponential backoff and idempotency. For user-facing keep retries minimal to avoid worsening user latency. We'll send a short doc with concrete numbers.
39:55 James Liu: Any compliance or PII risk due to added tracing? We need to ensure no sensitive data ends up in traces.
41:05 Samira Shah: Tracing respects automatic redaction and you can set filters; we'll include the privacy and SOC2 notes in the doc.
42:50 Alex Kim: Quick recap: Redwood to send incident timeline & postmortem, client retry patch PR and recommended backoff config, tracing docs; Lumina to run staging load test and share logs; follow-up sync 2026-05-13 16:00 UTC.
45:10 Mark Rivera: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
46:00 Priya Desai: Thanks, bye.
meeting_notes: Recap: Monday incident caused timeouts and 5xx spike; root cause: scheduled embeddings job caused KV cache evictions and memory pressure
Mitigations applied: edge rate limiter, autoscaler threshold change, client retry guidance, temporary memory cap hotfix

Recommendations: isolate embeddings route/dedicated pool or quantized variant, implement jittered exponential backoff, per-route rate limits and burst tokens, increase tracing sampling for failed requests
Next: Redwood to share postmortem + retry PR + tracing docs; Lumina to run staging stress test and share logs; follow-up on 2026-05-13 16:00 UTC
